# Omnix

> Omnix is NixOS with the standard Linux filesystem layout. That layout is a layer of symlinks and a library cache over unmodified nixpkgs — nothing is forked, overlaid or patched — so Omarchy's Hyprland desktop, KDE Plasma - Atrium and prebuilt Linux software run as-is, with declarative configuration and boot-menu rollbacks.

- Base: NixOS (nixos-unstable), unmodified. Packages stay as-is in /nix/store and download from cache.nixos.org; Omnix adds only filesystem layout (symlinks, a library cache), so there are no overlays, no patched packages and no fork.
- Compatibility layer: nix-ld (the /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 loader), envfs (/usr/bin, /bin), and a Nix-managed /usr/lib.
- Installer: ISO v0.1.0 for x86-64 PCs; run `sudo omnix-install` and choose a disk, encryption and desktop.
- Desktops ("flavors"):
  - Hyprland - Omarchy: an independent port of Omarchy. Runs Omarchy's own Hyprland config, keybindings, themes and scripts; maps 131 of its 147 base packages. `stable` pins Omarchy 4.0.4, `latest` follows its development branch.
  - KDE Plasma - Atrium: a declarative, mouse-first KDE Plasma 6 desktop that borrows Omarchy habits (Meta+W overview, per-screen desktops, JetBrainsMono Nerd Font, fast key repeat).
  - Minimal: the base alone.
- Rollback: every system update is a boot-menu entry. Rolling back restores system apps, libraries, settings and the compatibility layer; files and personal settings in the home folder are not changed.
- Themes: Hyprland - Omarchy includes Omarchy's built-in themes (Tokyo Night, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Nord, Rosé Pine and more); Super + Ctrl + Shift + Space switches theme immediately, with no rebuild.
- Omarchy Plugins: upstream supports bar widgets, panels, background services and replacement bars. The Hyprland flavor includes the host; verified plugin lifecycle support on Omnix is under development. Plugins run with user access, and system rollback does not restore personal plugin files. KDE Plasma Wayland support would require an adapted host; native Plasma widget compatibility is not provided, and Hyprland-dependent plugins need porting.
- Switching desktops: the installed system is a flake the user owns in /etc/nixos; the desktop is one input in it. Change it and rebuild; the previous desktop stays in the boot menu.
- Independent: not affiliated with or endorsed by Omarchy, 37signals, Basecamp or the NixOS Foundation.

## Links

- [Website](https://www.omnix-linux.com/)
- [Omnix base and installer](https://github.com/Omnix-Linux/Omnix)
- [Installer ISO releases](https://github.com/Omnix-Linux/Omnix/releases)
- [Report a bug](https://github.com/Omnix-Linux/Omnix/issues/new?template=bug.yml): one form for the installer, base, desktops and local AI
- [Soldr](https://github.com/zackees/soldr): on Omnix, `cargo` is aliased to `soldr cargo`, so the usual commands drive a build that fetches and pins the right toolchain and caches every compilation. The cache is content-addressed and shared across branches and pull requests, for roughly 2x faster cross-PR builds, Cross-compilation is a first-class citizen: the tools are built in, so one command cross-compiles a macOS binary from Linux (also `win-x64`, `linux-x64-musl`) without renting a runner. Developed by the same person behind Omnix. Beta software; pin the release.
- [Hyprland - Omarchy flavor](https://github.com/Omnix-Linux/Autarchy)
- [Omarchy Plugins section](https://www.omnix-linux.com/#plugins)
- [Plugin support research and roadmap](https://github.com/Omnix-Linux/Autarchy/issues/2)
- [KDE Plasma - Atrium flavor](https://github.com/Omnix-Linux/Atrium)
- [Try Omnix Docker app](https://github.com/Omnix-Linux/docker-vm/blob/feat/omnix-demo/docs/OMNIX.md)

## Coming next

Running prebuilt software already works out of the box: the base ships a loader, so ordinary Linux programs run unmodified. The planned work covers the two kinds that need no Linux binary at all.

- Built-in support for Actually Portable Executables (APE): Cosmopolitan-style single-file programs, one file that runs on many operating systems, treated as first-class apps.
- A WebAssembly runtime for micro apps: small sandboxed WASM modules on a stable kernel API, aiming for near-native speed.
